name: @tanqory/theme-mcp

tools.name: theme_guide
tools.description: Explains, step by step and with examples, how to build or restyle your store theme with AI. Read it before starting a theme.

tools.name: theme_reference
tools.description: Reads one reference of the theme rules, such as every section and setting a theme can use.

name.description: theme-schema, theme-setting-types, theme-limits, theme-assets, nova-v3-catalogue (every section and block), nova-v3-settings, nova-v3-templates or theme-guide. The same documents are MCP resources.

tools.name: theme_validate
tools.description: Checks a theme for problems and says how to fix each one, before anything is saved. It changes nothing.

files.description: Theme files by path, each the full text: templates/<name>.json, groups/<name>.json, config/settings.json. Give files or dir. Every problem comes back with file, line, column and fix; at most 25 sections per template, blocks 8 levels deep. Checks the packaged Nova offline; theme_push_draft checks again against the store's installed build.

dir.description: A theme folder on this machine (config/, groups/, templates/); relative to the working directory.

tools.name: theme_init
tools.description: Gives the starter files of the Nova base theme to build a new theme from. It never overwrites a file you already have.

dir.description: A theme folder on this machine (config/, groups/, templates/); relative to the working directory. With dir, the starter files are written into it, never over an existing file; without it, the core files are returned.

paths.description: Without dir: the starter files to return in full (by default config/settings.json, groups/header.json, groups/footer.json, templates/index.json).

tools.name: theme_get
tools.description: Lists your store's themes and shows which one is live and which are drafts.

themeId.description: One theme; leave out to list them all. Needs tanqory-theme login once.

tools.name: theme_files
tools.description: Reads the content of one of your themes: its settings, header, footer and page templates. It can also save them into a folder on this computer.

themeId.description: A theme of the store, from theme_get.

paths.description: Only these files, e.g. templates/index.json; leave out for all.

dir.description: A theme folder on this machine (config/, groups/, templates/); relative to the working directory. With dir, the files are also written into it, replacing what is there.

tools.name: theme_push_draft
tools.description: Saves theme changes as a draft, never touching your live theme. You approve the change before it is saved.

files.description: Theme files by path, each the full text: templates/<name>.json, groups/<name>.json, config/settings.json. Give files or dir. Validated here first, then by the cloud; a theme that does not pass is refused with every finding.

dir.description: A theme folder on this machine (config/, groups/, templates/); relative to the working directory.

themeId.description: A draft this connection made (theme_get shows madeByThisConnection). Leave out to make a new draft.

confirmationToken.description: Leave out on the first call: it changes nothing and returns the change with a confirmationToken. After the merchant approves that change, call again with the same arguments and this token to make it.

annotations.title: Save a theme as a draft

tools.name: theme_preview_url
tools.description: Gives a private link to preview a draft theme before it goes live. The link stays the same when the draft changes.

themeId.description: A theme that is not live, from theme_get. While the preview is being prepared the answer has status "pending": ask again after a few seconds. Give the merchant previewLink: it stays the same after every push. url opens this version only.

tools.name: theme_preview_screenshot
tools.description: Takes desktop and mobile pictures of a draft theme, so the AI can check its work before you see it. It changes nothing.

themeId.description: A draft you pushed (theme_push_draft answers it). The answer holds images, desktop 1440 wide and mobile 390 wide, rendered by the cloud. Call this after every push, compare the images with the request, fix what differs and push again with the same themeId, then give the merchant previewLink.

template.description: A page with a fixed address; default index (the home page).

path.description: Any other page by its address on the store, starting with "/", e.g. "/products/<handle>". Instead of template.

fullPage.description: The whole page instead of the first screen. Default false.

tools.name: theme_upload_asset
tools.description: Adds an image to your store's files so your theme can use it. You approve each upload, and its licence must allow commercial use.

source.description: { "url": "https://…" } that another tool gave, or { "path": "hero.webp" }, a file on this machine of at most 3 MiB. PNG, JPEG or WebP. The answer has the https URL to put in an image setting.

alt.description: What the image shows, for people who cannot see it.

licence.description: How the file may be used. kind: owned, ai-generated, cc0, cc-by-4.0, licensed; it must allow commercial use.

confirmationToken.description: Leave out on the first call: it changes nothing and returns the change with a confirmationToken. After the merchant approves that change, call again with the same arguments and this token to make it.

annotations.title: Add an image to your files

tools.name: theme_publish
tools.description: Makes a draft theme your live theme once you've seen its preview. You approve it before shoppers see it.

themeId.description: A draft this connection made with theme_push_draft, after the merchant saw its preview and asked to publish it.

confirmationToken.description: Leave out on the first call: it changes nothing and returns the change with a confirmationToken. After the merchant approves that change, call again with the same arguments and this token to make it.

tools.name: theme_submit_check
tools.description: Lists every problem a partner theme would meet when it is uploaded and checked, each with the file, the rule, why and how to fix it. It changes nothing.

dir.description: The partner theme folder on this machine (its package.json, src/, scripts/build.mjs …), as create-tanqory-theme or tanqory-partner theme init made it. Relative to the working directory. The theme's own build runs here (npm install first). The source layout is checked with the rules the upload gate reads; the nine checks that need no sandbox and the sandbox ones this machine can run (two builds compared, entry imports, static size budgets, network origins) run with the platform's own code from @tanqory/partner-cli, each sandbox one labelled "local result". Answers ready, problems[{file, rule, why, fix}], lines, leftOut (files the upload leaves out).

annotations.title: Check a partner theme before you submit

tools.name: theme_submit_prepare
tools.description: Builds a partner theme and writes the archive and manifest the Upload Version form takes, leaving out editor and AI assistant files. It never deletes or changes your files.

dir.description: The partner theme folder, as for theme_submit_check. It runs that check first: while a problem remains that only you can fix (a refused file, a package.json rule, a missing LICENSE), no archive is written and every problem is listed. Otherwise it writes <name>-<version>.tgz (files at its root; editor, AI assistant, test, CI and macOS files and lockfiles left out) and <name>-<version>.manifest.json, and answers the next steps: upload, Install on Dev Store, wait for 15 of 15, Submit for Review.

outDir.description: Where to write the two files; default dist/partner in the theme folder.

annotations.title: Prepare a partner theme for upload

instructions: Build Tanqory store themes: read theme_guide first. Themes are content for the Nova V3 base theme and must pass theme_validate before they are pushed or published. Every tool that changes the store (theme_push_draft, theme_upload_asset, theme_publish) takes two calls: the first changes nothing and returns the change and a confirmationToken; show that change to the merchant, and only after they approve it call the same tool again with the same arguments and the token. Partner themes (a theme folder with its own build file, for the Theme Store): run theme_submit_check on the folder, fix every problem it lists (file, rule, why, fix), run it again until ready, then theme_submit_prepare writes the archive and manifest for Upload Version and lists the next steps. Tools that read or change the store need a sign-in once (tanqory-theme login). Push a draft (never the live theme), look at it with theme_preview_screenshot and fix what differs from the request, push a follow-up change with the same themeId, give the merchant the previewLink of theme_preview_url, and publish only when the merchant asks.
